subsection_title: Dominant classes are highly stable within pairs
figure_title: Dominant ratio class and seed agreement across pairs
legend_explanation: Blue, gold, and orange cells denote ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC. Each cell prints the dominant class letter and the percentage of fitting seeds assigned to that class. Column labels identify the pair and its ploidy category.
result_interpretation: Use the class labels to locate consistent in-vivo decreases, approximate coupling, and increases before examining continuous ratio magnitude.
limitation_note: A dominant class summarizes 500 optimization seeds; it does not make those seeds independent biological replicates.

subsection_title: Continuous ratios reveal magnitude hidden by class labels
figure_title: Pair-by-parameter log2 in-vivo/in-vitro ratio landscape
legend_explanation: Blue tiles are negative log2 ratios, white is ratio 1, and orange tiles are positive log2 ratios. Printed signed values are pair-level median log2 ratios; color intensity is symmetric around zero.
result_interpretation: Read this map before the class matrix when the size of the in-vivo/in-vitro difference matters, because two values in the same class may have very different magnitudes.
limitation_note: Color saturation is bounded for readability, so use the printed value or source table for exact extremes.

subsection_title: Seed composition identifies strict and mixed classifications
figure_title: Within-pair ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC seed composition
legend_explanation: Each horizontal stacked bar represents all available seeds for one pair and parameter and sums to 100%. Blue is ClassA, gold is ClassB, and orange is ClassC; ClassB uses 1/1.1 to 1.1.
result_interpretation: Bars concentrated in one color indicate numerical stability across optimizer initializations; mixed bars identify threshold-crossing solutions.
limitation_note: Seed composition measures fitting stability within a pair, not population prevalence.

subsection_title: Entropy isolates seed-sensitive parameter calls
figure_title: Normalized class entropy within each pair
legend_explanation: Cells range from light for entropy 0 to dark gold for entropy 1. Printed values are normalized entropy: 0 means every seed has one class, whereas 1 is the maximum A/B/C mixture.
result_interpretation: Low entropy confirms that a parameter's class is insensitive to optimizer initialization within the pair.
limitation_note: Entropy does not indicate whether the dominant class is biologically correct or whether the estimate is identifiable.

subsection_title: Union, graded cores, and intersections separate weak from strict membership
figure_title: Union, stable-core, and strict-intersection membership by class
legend_explanation: Columns are ratio classes and cells are colored by the strongest membership level: union, stable-80, stable-90, stable-95, or strict 100% intersection. Printed percentages give the seed proportion in that class for the pair and parameter.
result_interpretation: This hierarchy distinguishes a parameter observed in a class at least once from one assigned to the same class in every seed.
limitation_note: The stability cutoffs are descriptive thresholds and should be interpreted with the continuous ratio distribution.

subsection_title: ClassB can still be directionally asymmetric around ratio 1
figure_title: Direction of ratios inside the ClassB coupling band
legend_explanation: Only ClassB seeds are included. Blue denotes ratios below 1, the neutral fill denotes ratio exactly 1, and orange denotes ratios above 1; each bar is the directional composition among ClassB seeds.
result_interpretation: A parameter may satisfy the coupling band while consistently lying on one side of equality, revealing residual directional asymmetry.
limitation_note: Parameters without ClassB seeds are omitted, and direction within the band should not be mistaken for a large effect.

subsection_title: Distributions show whether class calls are compact or cutoff driven
figure_title: Seed-level log2 ratio distributions within each pair
legend_explanation: Blue violins show the full seed distribution, white boxes show the median and interquartile range, the black vertical line is ratio 1 on the log2 scale, and the gold vertical band marks ClassB between log2(1/1.1) and log2(1.1).
result_interpretation: Compact distributions far from the gold band support stable ClassA or ClassC calls; distributions touching a cutoff require more cautious classification.
limitation_note: Very narrow violins can reflect optimizer convergence as well as limited parameter uncertainty.

subsection_title: Consensus distinguishes pair-specific from cross-pair classes
figure_title: Cross-pair dominant-class consensus by parameter
legend_explanation: Point color gives the cross-pair dominant class: blue ClassA, gold ClassB, or orange ClassC. Horizontal position is the fraction of pairs sharing that class, labels give the exact count out of six, and vertical guides mark 80%, 90%, and 95%.
result_interpretation: Parameters at six of six pairs provide the clearest evidence for a directionally consistent in-vivo/in-vitro shift.
limitation_note: Only six pairs are available, so one pair changes the consensus fraction by 16.7 percentage points.

subsection_title: Pair-balanced rankings compare all three classes on equal footing
figure_title: Pair-balanced ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC parameter rankings
legend_explanation: The three panels correspond to ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC. Points are pair-balanced mean seed proportions and gray horizontal intervals are 95% pair-bootstrap intervals; panel colors follow the class palette.
result_interpretation: Rankings identify which parameters most consistently occupy each class without allowing pairs with more seeds to dominate.
limitation_note: Bootstrap intervals resample only six pairs and therefore describe sensitivity to the observed pairs rather than a population-level certainty bound.

subsection_title: Stable-90 coverage identifies the broadest cross-pair cores
figure_title: Cross-pair stable-90 core coverage
legend_explanation: Each panel is one ratio class. The point and direct label give how many of six pairs have at least 90% of seeds in that class; the gray segment connects zero to the observed pair count.
result_interpretation: Six of six marks a parameter that is seed-stable in the same class across every available pair.
limitation_note: The 90% rule is a prespecified descriptive cutoff and does not test biological replication.

subsection_title: Pair intervals expose direction, magnitude, and seed spread
figure_title: Pair-specific log2 ratio medians and seed intervals
legend_explanation: Points show the median log2 in-vivo/in-vitro ratio, gray horizontal intervals span the 5th to 95th seed percentiles, and point fill gives the dominant class. The black vertical line is ratio 1 and the gold band is ClassB.
result_interpretation: This forest view shows whether cross-pair class disagreement reflects genuinely different effect directions or values near a cutoff.
limitation_note: Intervals summarize optimization seeds within a pair and are not confidence intervals for independent biological samples.

subsection_title: Parameter-level profiles connect classes to model mechanisms
figure_title: Soft-coupling classes grouped by biological process
legend_explanation: Rows are parameters grouped by their audited primary process and columns are ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC. Gold intensity and printed percentages give the pair-balanced seed proportion assigned to each class.
result_interpretation: The map links consistent coupling behavior to hypoxia sensing, growth, death, CIN, WGD, and post-missegregation buffering mechanisms.
limitation_note: Process labels come from the model parameter table; class association alone does not establish a causal biological mechanism.

subsection_title: Process averages summarize direction but can hide parameter heterogeneity
figure_title: Pair-balanced class profile by biological process
legend_explanation: Panels correspond to ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC. Each point is the mean pair-balanced seed proportion across parameters in the process, with class-specific point colors and gray segments from zero.
result_interpretation: Use this summary to compare broad process tendencies, then return to the parameter map to identify which parameter drives the average.
limitation_note: Processes contain different numbers and roles of parameters, so their averages are descriptive rather than directly comparable effect sizes.

subsection_title: Each pair has one stable ploidy category
figure_title: Ploidy-trajectory category assignment for each pair
legend_explanation: Point color identifies CatA, CatB, CatC, or CatU. Horizontal position is the fraction of seeds assigned to the pair's dominant category, and labels report the category and exact seed agreement.
result_interpretation: The figure verifies that all 500 seeds within each pair receive the same primary ploidy category.
limitation_note: Because no pair contains multiple categories, within-pair CatA/B/C effects are not estimable.

subsection_title: Archetypes distinguish maintained, one-stage, and two-stage decline
figure_title: Pair-balanced CatA, CatB, and CatC ploidy trajectories
legend_explanation: Teal, orange, and purple curves denote CatA, CatB, and CatC. Ribbons span the 25th to 75th percentile of pair medians; panels separate 2N and 4N cohorts. Dashed and dotted horizontal lines mark chromosome numbers 44 and 22.
result_interpretation: The archetypes provide the operational trajectory shapes used to interpret category-specific parameter patterns.
limitation_note: Each category contains two pairs, so ribbons summarize the observed pair medians rather than a broad biological population.

subsection_title: Pair trajectories confirm reproducibility without merging cohorts
figure_title: Pair-specific 0-1000 day ploidy trajectories
legend_explanation: Line and ribbon color identifies the assigned ploidy category. Lines are seed medians, ribbons are seed interquartile ranges, columns are pairs, and rows separate 2N and 4N cohorts. Horizontal references mark 44 and 22 chromosomes.
result_interpretation: This view checks whether the category label reflects both initial-ploidy cohorts and whether the trajectory is reproducible across seeds.
limitation_note: The displayed spread is within-pair simulation variation conditional on fitted parameters.

subsection_title: Representative trajectories make detected transitions auditable
figure_title: Representative trajectories with detected drop starts
legend_explanation: Curve color identifies the ploidy category. One deterministic representative seed is shown per pair and cohort; dashed and dotted vertical lines mark the first and second detected drop starts, while horizontal references mark 44 and 22 chromosomes.
result_interpretation: The representative traces provide a direct visual audit of the automated one-stage versus two-stage transition calls.
limitation_note: One representative seed cannot display the full within-pair spread and must be read alongside the pair trajectory summary.

subsection_title: Plateau duration and model support separate CatB from CatC
figure_title: CatB/C transition diagnostics
legend_explanation: Each point is one pair by seed by initial cohort. Color identifies the assigned category and shape identifies 2N or 4N. The vertical guide is a 60-day plateau and the horizontal guide is delta BIC of -10; CatC support lies to the right and below these guides.
result_interpretation: The joint diagnostic tests whether a delayed second decline is supported by both plateau duration and stronger two-transition fit.
limitation_note: Threshold proximity indicates sensitivity, and the plotted categories remain model-derived rather than experimentally observed states.

subsection_title: Cat-by-Class profiles identify candidate category-specific coupling patterns
figure_title: Pair-balanced CatA/B/C by ClassA/B/C profile
legend_explanation: Rows are parameters and columns are Cat-by-Class combinations. Gold intensity and printed percentages give the mean seed proportion after weighting each contributing pair equally.
result_interpretation: The matrix highlights parameters whose coupling class changes across ploidy categories while avoiding seed-level pseudoreplication.
limitation_note: Each Cat contains only two pairs, and category is confounded with pair identity.

subsection_title: Effect-size rankings are descriptive with six pair-level observations
figure_title: Pair-level Cat-by-dominant-class association strength
legend_explanation: Gold points show descriptive pair-level Cramer's V from zero to one and gray segments connect zero to the observed value. Parameters with no class variation have no estimable Cramer's V.
result_interpretation: Higher values flag candidate parameters whose dominant class pattern differs across CatA, CatB, and CatC.
limitation_note: With six pairs and no within-pair category variation, the statistic cannot separate category effects from pair effects and should not be treated as inferential evidence.

subsection_title: Continuous ratios show category differences hidden by classes
figure_title: Soft-coupling ratio intervals within each ploidy category
legend_explanation: Panels separate CatA, CatB, and CatC. Points show pair-balanced mean log2 ratios, gray intervals span the two observed pair values, the black vertical line is ratio 1, and the gold band is ClassB.
result_interpretation: This figure compares effect magnitude across categories and prevents categorical thresholds from hiding large within-class differences.
limitation_note: The interval is the observed range of two pairs, not a confidence interval.

subsection_title: Dumbbells localize whether category differences arise in vivo or in vitro
figure_title: In-vivo and in-vitro parameter values by ploidy category
legend_explanation: Circles are pair-balanced in-vitro values and triangles are pair-balanced in-vivo values; connecting segments and colors identify CatA, CatB, and CatC. Each parameter has its own panel and the x-axis is log10 scaled.
result_interpretation: The endpoints distinguish changes in the in-vivo fit from changes in the shared in-vitro anchor.
limitation_note: Free x-scales support within-parameter comparison but do not permit visual magnitude comparison across different parameter panels.

subsection_title: The two contributing pairs reveal hidden category disagreement
figure_title: Pair-level ratios underlying each ploidy category
legend_explanation: Each point is one pair and shape identifies the pair. Point fill identifies CatA, CatB, or CatC, gray intervals span the 5th to 95th seed percentiles, the black line is ratio 1, and the gold band is ClassB.
result_interpretation: Pair-level detail shows whether a category average is supported by both pairs or driven by one contributor.
limitation_note: Only two pairs contribute to each category, so apparent agreement or disagreement has limited replication.

subsection_title: Threshold grids distinguish robust classes from cutoff artifacts
figure_title: ClassA/B/C sensitivity to the ratio threshold
legend_explanation: Panels separate ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC. Rows are parameters, columns are symmetric ratio thresholds, and gold intensity is the pair-balanced seed proportion assigned to the class; 1.1 is the primary threshold.
result_interpretation: Stable color across nearby thresholds supports robust classification, whereas abrupt changes identify cutoff-dependent calls.
limitation_note: Sensitivity to a cutoff does not indicate which threshold is biologically optimal.

subsection_title: Objective strata test whether poor fits drive class patterns
figure_title: ClassA/B/C robustness across objective-quality subsets
legend_explanation: Panels separate the three classes. Columns are all seeds, near-optimal subsets, top-percentile subsets, and the best seed; blue intensity gives pair-balanced class proportion.
result_interpretation: Agreement across objective strata indicates that the class pattern is not driven by worse-fitting seeds.
limitation_note: The best-seed stratum contains only one seed per pair and is therefore intrinsically less stable than broader subsets.

subsection_title: Boundary diagnostics flag potentially constrained estimates
figure_title: Boundary, projection, and feasibility diagnostics
legend_explanation: Facets show projection use, feasibility before projection, feasibility at the solution, and whether any bound is active. Each tile is a pair-parameter summary and orange intensity gives the fraction of seeds with the diagnostic.
result_interpretation: High active-bound or projection rates identify parameter interpretations that require identifiability caution.
limitation_note: The any-bound diagnostic is solution-level and does not by itself prove that the displayed parameter is the one on a bound.

subsection_title: Membership matrices identify the exact pairs behind stable cores
figure_title: Stable-90 pair-set membership by class
legend_explanation: Panels separate ClassA, ClassB, and ClassC. Rows are pairs, columns are parameters, and a filled gold dot means at least 90% of that pair's seeds belong to the displayed class.
result_interpretation: The matrix reveals whether a reported cross-pair core is broad or depends on a specific subset of pairs.
limitation_note: Membership is binary at the 90% cutoff and should be checked against the underlying proportions near that boundary.

subsection_title: Signed margins locate trajectories close to category cutoffs
figure_title: Ploidy classification margins relative to primary cutoffs
legend_explanation: Boxes summarize signed distances from each classification cutoff, with panels for different diagnostics. Blue and orange fills distinguish 2N and 4N cohorts, and the vertical zero line marks the decision boundary.
result_interpretation: Distributions far from zero support stable classification; values near zero identify trajectories that may switch under small threshold changes.
limitation_note: The biological interpretation of positive versus negative differs by diagnostic, so compare distance from zero rather than sign across panels.

subsection_title: Category assignments remain stable across the prespecified grid
figure_title: Ploidy-category sensitivity across 81 threshold scenarios
legend_explanation: Each stacked bar represents one pair across 81 prespecified scenarios. Teal, orange, purple, and gray denote CatA, CatB, CatC, and CatU; the annotation reports how often the primary category is retained.
result_interpretation: A bar concentrated in the primary color indicates that the Cat assignment is insensitive to the tested cutoff grid.
limitation_note: Robustness is limited to the prespecified scenarios and does not cover alternative classification algorithms.
